name: Fondue
description:
A swiss classic for cold winter dinners.
Traditionally cooked in a “Caquelon” pot and served on a candle heated stove, to keep the cheese from going solid again.

ingredients.name: Swiss cheese
ingredients.originalText: 800 g (1.7 lbs) swiss cheese (50/50 mix of Gruyère and Emmentaler recommended)
ingredients.preparation: 1.7 lbs; 50/50 mix of Gruyère and Emmentaler recommended

instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: 1 garlic clove; 4 dl (1.5 cups) white wine; 800 g (1.7 lbs) swiss cheese (50/50 mix of Gruyère and Emmentaler recommended); 1 shot of kirsch (cherry brandy); 1 tsp lemon juice; 1-2 tbsp starch flour; 1 loaf (~800g/~1.7 lbs) of white bread; A pinch of nutmeg. Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Set out the bowls, pans, measuring tools, and any baking equipment named in the steps below. Wash any fresh produce before use. Keep raw eggs, meat, and their utensils separate from ready-to-eat food.
Rub the Pot with garlic clove.
Put cheese, starch, wine and lemon juice in pot and melt while stiring constantly.
Season with a bit of pepper and nutmeg.
Stick bread squares on fondue fork one by one and stir them in the fondue.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.

source.author: sekthor
source.originalInstructions:
1. Rub the Pot with garlic clove.
2. Cut bread into small squares.
3. Put cheese, starch, wine and lemon juice in pot and melt while stiring constantly.
4. Season with a bit of pepper and nutmeg.
5. Serve right away.
6. Stick bread squares on fondue fork one by one and stir them in the fondue.
